sentences.text: This large marine crocodile-like reptile had a partial jaw that was deeper than those of its close relatives.
Its teeth were large and curved backward, featuring circular cross-sections, smooth edges, and vertical grooves.
The leg bones measured 36 centimeters and 21 centimeters in length.
One tail bone possessed a notably larger spine, suggesting a rudimentary vertical tail expansion.
Armor plates covered its back and belly in two dorsal rows and at least two ventral rows.
Scientists first described this extinct genus from fossils found in the Kisgerecse Marl Formation in Hungary.
A fragmentary skeleton was uncovered in 1996.
Because of its large size and unique trait combination, this animal represents a transitional form between fully marine relatives and their earlier non-marine ancestors.
It holds the distinction of being the earliest known thalattosuchian adapted to open-ocean conditions instead of coastal or lagoonal habitats.
Taxonomically, it belongs to the superfamily Metriorhynchoidea and the suborder Thalattosuchia.
Fossils from the Kisgerecse Marl Formation indicate an open-ocean environment during the Toarcian stage, from 180.4 to 174.7 million years ago.
